requirements.evidence: All contract members are present: Queues.php has name/creating/viewingQueueId/confirmingToggle/editingQueueId/renameName/accessQueueId/managingAccess and every listed method; render passes accessQueue (scoped find) and accessGrants (collect() when null). rename() passes `slug: Str::slug($this->renameName)`; create() maps domain slug errors to `name` via surfaceValidationError. The toggle uses an in-page modal (queues.blade.php:134-158), not wire:confirm. Serve.php: `#[Locked] public ?int $lastCalledTicketId`, mount defaults to the first callable queue, callNext handles a null selection, does a scoped findOrFail, catches InactiveQueueException and NoWaitingTicketsException, does not catch the authorization exception, and rate-limits only successful calls (10/min). The waiting list is ordered priority desc, issued_at, id, filtered by mode, limited to 30, and empty when the user cannot call the queue. Members has activeTab/setActiveTab with a whitelist and a role="tablist" bar, and the invite form renders only on the invites tab. Routes and navbar entries (with @can create Queue for managers) are added, and every lang key exists in both locales.

conventions.evidence: Writes go through CreateQueue/UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess/CallNextTicket. #[Validate] + validateOnly is used for name, renameName and mode. CHANGELOG.md and docs/business-rules.md are updated. Deviations: grantAccess()/revokeAccess() (Queues.php) call no `$this->authorize(...)` and rely on the action's internal check, against Livewire policy rule 3. Role logic is in a Blade `@php` block (`in_array($membership->role, [\App\Models\UserRole::Owner, ...])`, queues.blade.php ~line 174). There are many inline `style=` attributes instead of a reusable Blade component for the modal and row markup.

security.evidence: Every client id is resolved with `$this->entity->queues()->findOrFail(...)` / `memberships()->findOrFail(...)`. The entity and lastCalledTicketId are #[Locked]. mode is validated before `CallMode::from`. The view uses {{ }} escaping only. A tampered accessQueueId gives accessQueue null and empty grants. The serve preview checks `Gate::allows('call', $selectedQueue)` before listing tickets, and call-next is rate-limited. Gap with limited impact: grantAccess/revokeAccess have no component-level authorize. They are still guarded by SetQueueAccess's internal authorization, so this is not exploitable as shown.

tests.evidence: QueuesTest covers employee 403 (route + component), no row actions in the list HTML, create with slug derivation and duplicate error, detail/close resets, rename with slug and collision, the toggle confirm modal and the absence of wire:confirm, grant/revoke, the navbar, and foreign queue/membership/accessQueueId tampering. ServeTest covers default selection, employee filtering, ordering/mode/channel translation, the 30 cap, success, empty, inactive, unauthorized employee 403 with no disclosure, invalid mode, foreign id and rate limit. MembersTabsTest covers the tabs. Missing: an employee calling each Queues action directly (create, rename, toggleActive, grantAccess, etc.) to show it is denied. Only mount is tested for employees. There is also no test that the access audit log is written, even though a test name claims it.

simplicity.evidence: Components are direct and reuse the domain actions. There is some redundancy: Serve::render passes each collection twice ('callableQueues' and 'queues', 'tickets' and 'waitingTickets'). queues.blade.php duplicates the revoke button in the manager and granted branches and the active/inactive tag markup in the list and the detail modal. rename() falls back to `$this->editingQueueId ?? $this->viewingQueueId ?? 0`, which adds a path nobody needs.

readability.evidence: Names are clear, methods are small and documented ("Untrusted client state — always re-resolved scoped"), and the code follows the Members component style. The Blade files are long and full of inline flex styles, and the extra view-data aliases make it less clear which one the template uses.

scope.evidence: Adds `.github/workflows/deploy-dev.yml` (a deploy-on-push to main workflow using HOSTINGER_API/APP_KEY/DB_PASSWORD secrets) and `.github/workflows/tests.yml`. Neither relates to the queues/serve/tabs task. Everything else (the sendInvite tab switch and the test updates for the tabbed members page) serves the task.

issues.explanation: These add CI and deploy-to-VPS workflows (including a deploy that triggers on push to main), which the UI task did not ask for and which change infrastructure behaviour.

Public actions call no `$this->authorize('manageAccess', $queue)` and rely only on SetQueueAccess's internal check, which breaks the Livewire policy rule that every public method authorizes server-side.

The convention requires an unauthorized-call test for each action, but the tests never show an employee calling create/rename/toggleActive/grantAccess/revokeAccess directly and being denied; only mount is covered.

issues.location: tests/Feature/Entity/QueuesTest.php ('queue access can be granted and revoked with an audit write')
issues.explanation: The test title claims an audit write, but nothing asserts that the audit log entry is produced.
The role check (owner/admin) is done in a Blade `@php` block instead of being computed in the component or a policy.
Each collection is passed under two names ('queues'/'callableQueues', 'waitingTickets'/'tickets'), which adds view data nobody needs.
The revoke button markup is duplicated in the manager and granted branches, and the status tag markup is repeated.
Falling back from editingQueueId to viewingQueueId means rename() can act without startRename having been called, which is surprising for readers.

review.summary: The change adds the Queues management and Serve Livewire panels, the members tabs, routes, navbar entries, lang keys, docs and comprehensive Pest tests. It meets the task contract with careful entity-scoped id resolution and good tamper tests. It also ships unrelated GitHub CI/deploy workflows, which must be removed before merging. Grant/revoke skip component-level authorization, and there are no per-action unauthorized-call tests, so the PR needs changes.
